evals.prompt:
Write the Claude tool definition for this Python function in our Acme order service:

def search_orders(customer_id: str, status: str | None = None, placed_after: str | None = None, sort: str = 'desc', limit: int = 20):
    """Find a customer's orders. status is one of pending, shipped, delivered, cancelled. placed_after is an ISO date. sort is by order date, asc or desc. limit 1-100."""

The agent also has a separate get_order(order_id) tool, so the descriptions need to keep them apart.
assertions: Produces a valid Anthropic tool definition with name, description, and input_schema of type object
The top-level description names a decision condition (when to call search_orders versus get_order), not just a restatement of the function name
A required array is present and contains customer_id; every name in required exists in properties
Every parameter has a non-empty description, and limit states its valid range (1-100)
The status and sort enums list their values with a one-phrase explanation of each value
Includes a Python snippet passing the tool to client.messages.create(tools=[...]) and handling stop_reason == 'tool_use'
Does not invent parameters, enum values, or behaviors not in the supplied signature and docstring
